SMTO-JOB-0005 — The terminal can't open on this computer

GUID: 06d4b787-8073-4343-93b0-e7809f450ceb
Slug: terminal-unsupported
Domain: JOB · Subsystem: job

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't open a live terminal on this computer. Gateways running directly on Windows don't support it yet, or the page sent a request the Gateway didn't understand.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the Gateway computer runs Windows, ask SMTO in the conversation to run the commands you need instead of using the terminal. SMTO can still run commands and show their output on Windows; only the live terminal is missing.
  2. If you need a live terminal on that Windows computer, ask the person who installed SMTO to set up the Linux Gateway inside WSL there. The Linux Gateway supports live terminals and can run inside WSL on Windows.
  3. If the Gateway computer doesn't run Windows, reload this page and open the terminal again. An older copy of the page can send requests the Gateway no longer understands.
  4. If the terminal still won't open, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check for updates. SMTO and the Gateway need matching versions to talk to each other correctly.

What success looks like

  • The terminal opens and shows a prompt, or SMTO runs your commands in the conversation and shows their output.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO, saying which computer and operating system the Gateway runs on.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway rejected the interactive terminal: native Windows Gateways do not support terminal sessions, or the terminal connection received a message type other than input, resize or close.

What this means

  • The native Windows terminal implementation raises TerminalUnsupportedError, or the terminal websocket receives a message type other than input, resize or close. Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.

Why this can happen

  • The native Windows terminal implementation raises TerminalUnsupportedError, or the terminal websocket receives a message type other than input, resize or close.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish absent native platform support from an invalid websocket control type.

How to fix it

  • Native Windows Gateways raise TerminalUnsupportedError for interactive PTY sessions (gateway_core/terminal_windows.py); use captured execution (/exec or /exec/stream) or run the Linux Gateway inside WSL. The terminal websocket in gateway_core/app.py also rejects message types other than input, resize and close, which points to a page/Gateway version mismatch.
  • Use a supported terminal platform/mode, or correct the rejected control message to the advertised protocol.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported execution mode and advertised terminal message contract are used.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
